title: George Smith Eponym Canon, Records of the Past, Turin Canon, Sir Isaac Newton, Ussher, Justin, Suetonius/Herodian & Cradock

nodes.name: Assyrian Eponym Canon Synchronisms (George Smith 1875): Shalmaneser III (↔ Ahab & Jehu), Tiglath-Pileser III (↔ Uzziah/Menahem/Ahaz) & Sargon II (722 BCE Samaria)
nodes.role: Cuneiform Year-by-Year Lock Linking Biblical Kings of Israel & Judah with Assyria
sources: George Smith The Assyrian Eponym Canon (1875) pp. 10-77
nodes.notes: British Museum Assyriologist George Smith edits the limmu eponym canon from Shalmaneser III through Sennacherib and Esarhaddon, locking Biblical reigns (Ahab, Jehu, Uzziah, Menahem, Pekah, Ahaz, Hezekiah & Tirhakah) to astronomical & eponym dates.

nodes.name: Records of the Past Vols. 9 & 11 (Cuneiform & Phoenician): Rimmon-Nirari I, Khorsabad Palace, Sennacherib Nebbi Yunus (46 Cities of Hezekiah), Ashurbanipal & King Eshmunazar of Sidon
nodes.era: 1320–5th c. BCE (Records of the Past Vols. 9 & 11)
nodes.role: Primary Translated Assyrian, Babylonian & Phoenician Royal Inscriptions
sources: Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Oppert, Pinches, George Smith)
Records of the Past Vol. 11 (Sayce, Budge)
nodes.notes: Primary translations of Adad-nirari I (son of Pudil, grandson of Bel-nirari, great-grandson of Assur-uballit I), Sargon's Khorsabad Annals, Sennacherib's Bavian & Nebbi Yunus inscriptions (46 cities of Hezekiah & Luli/Tubali of Sidon), Ashurbanipal's Cylinder B, and Sidon King Eshmunazar's sarcophagus.

nodes.name: The Turin King-List / Royal Canon of Turin (Kim Ryholt): Gods → Spirit Kings (Ax.w / Shemsu-Hor) → Historical Human Pharaohs
nodes.role: Only Native Pre-Ptolemaic True Royal Canon of Ancient Egypt
sources: Kim Ryholt The Turin King-List (Papyrus Turin inv. 1874 verso)
nodes.notes: Ryholt analyzes the 19th-Dynasty Turin King-List structuring Egyptian kingship into three tiers: mythological gods (Cols. I-II, ending in Seth & Horus), spirit/demigod kings (Ax.w / Shemsu-Hor), and exact human pharaohs through the Second Intermediate Period.

nodes.name: Sir Isaac Newton's Chronology Amended (1728): Sesostris = Shishak (1 Kings 14), Canaanites Fleeing Joshua, Danaus & Nabonassar (747 BCE)
nodes.era: Newtonian Synchronism Model (Sir Isaac Newton 1728 pp. 9-93)
nodes.role: Sir Isaac Newton's Compression of Pagan Chronologies to Biblical Anchors
sources: Sir Isaac Newton The Chronology of Ancient Kingdoms Amended (1728) pp. 9-93
nodes.notes: Newton synchronizes Mediterranean antiquity to Scripture by identifying Egyptian conqueror Sesostris with Biblical Shishak (1 Kings 14), tracing the Canaanite flight from Joshua into Egypt and Greece (Danaus), and anchoring Babylon & Assyria at Pul (747 BCE) and Nabonassar.

nodes.name: Archbishop Ussher's Annals of the World (1658), Blair (1753), Guthrie (1764) & Betham Tables (1795): Universal Biblical-Classical Chronology (4004 BCE – 70 CE)
nodes.era: Universal Chronography (Ussher 1658 p. 7; Blair 1753; Guthrie 1764; Betham 1795)
nodes.role: Grand Comparative Synchronism Unifying Creation, Patriarchs, Egypt & Greece
sources: Archbishop James Ussher Annals of the World (1658) p. 7
nodes.notes: Ussher's Annals (with Blair's Tables, Guthrie & Gray's 13-volume Universal History, the Universal History of the Holy Bible & British Family Bible) align Creation (4004 BCE), the Flood, Abraham, Jacob, Sicyon/Argos (Aegialeus/Inachus), and Manetho's Hyksos Pharaohs into one continuous timeline.

nodes.name: Justin / Pompeius Trogus Book XXXVI (Pagan Roman Testimony): Damascus → Abraham → Israhel (Jacob) → Judah, Joseph in Egypt & Moses
nodes.era: 1st c. BCE / 2nd c. CE (Justin Epitome of Pompeius Trogus XXXVI.2)
nodes.role: Independent Greco-Roman Ethnographic Summary of Israelite Origins
sources: Justin / Pompeius Trogus Book XXXVI (Watson 1853 p. 245)
nodes.notes: Trogus & Justin independently attest Hebrew patriarchs as historical kings/rulers in Syria ('Damascus -> Azelus -> Adores -> Abraham -> Israhel' with ten/twelve sons, Judas, Joseph in Egyptian dreamcraft & magic, and Moses leading the Exodus).

nodes.name: Justin Book XLI (Scythian Origin of Parthia): Exiled Scythians ('Parthi') → King Arsaces I → Mithridates I → Phraates
nodes.era: 247 BCE – 20 CE (Justin Epitome Book XLI pp. 272-297)
nodes.role: Classical Testimony Tracing the Arsacid Parthian Empire to Scythia
sources: Justin / Pompeius Trogus Book XLI (Watson 1853 pp. 272-297)
nodes.notes: Justin Book XLI explains that the Parthians — rivals who divided the world with Rome — originated as 'Parthi' (exiles) from Scythia before rising under Arsaces I, Mithridates I, and Phraates.

nodes.name: Suetonius (Twelve Caesars), Pliny & Herodian: Commodus → Pertinax → Septimius Severus → Caracalla → Elagabalus → Severus Alexander
nodes.era: 49 BCE – 238 CE (Suetonius; Pliny; Herodian; Basil Kennett)
nodes.role: Julio-Claudian / Flavian Documentation & Severan Roman Emperors
sources: Suetonius Lives of the Twelve Caesars
Herodian History of the Roman Emperors (1689 / 1749)
nodes.notes: Combines Suetonius's biographies of the Twelve Caesars, Pliny's Panegyrick on Trajan, Kennett's Roman Antiquities, and Herodian's eyewitness narrative from Marcus Aurelius & Commodus through Pertinax, Septimius Severus (campaigns in Britain), Caracalla, Elagabalus, and Severus Alexander.

nodes.name: Herodotus (Egypt, Persia & Greece) & Polybius (Punic Wars / Scipio & Hannibal): Classical Mediterranean Synchronisms
nodes.era: 5th–2nd c. BCE (Herodotus Vols. 1-2; Polybius Books I-V)
nodes.role: Father of History (Egypt/Cyrus/Xerxes) & Carthage–Rome Constitutional Bridge
sources: Polybius General History in Five Books
nodes.notes: Anchors Achaemenid, Saitic Egyptian, and Ionian/Athenian lineages (Herodotus Vols. 1-2) alongside Polybius's analytical account of the Punic Wars uniting Barcid Carthage, Numidia, Hellenistic Macedon/Seleucids, and Republican Rome.

nodes.name: Cradock's Apostolical History (1672): Global Missions of the Apostles — Paul's 5 Journeys to Rome, Peter, James, John, Thomas & the Early Churches
nodes.role: Complete Narrative Chronotaxis of the Apostolic Era & Epistles
sources: Samuel Cradock The Apostolical History (1672) Preface
nodes.notes: Cradock maps all five missionary journeys of Apostle Paul (Syria, Cyprus, Galatia, Macedonia, Greece, Ephesus & Rome), alongside the churches founded by Peter, James, John, and the Twelve Apostles.
